newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end weaker in dull,rangebound trade.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end weaker in dull,rangebound trade.

text.p: FCOJ futures closed slightly lower on Friday, but activity was extremely thin and rangebound.
"It was a dead day today," said one trader. "September had a 70 point range, November had a 50 point range, there was not much action at all."
September settled down 0.30 cent at 75.55 cents a lb, having ranged from 76.20 to 75.50 cents. November sagged 0.40 cent, to 77.50 cents, while the rest of the board closed 0.20 to 0.50 cent weaker.
An estimated 1,500 lots changed hands on the day.
Just ahead of the day's close, the USDA forecast Brazilian 1997/98 orange juice production at a record 1.25 million tonnes, up slightly from an earlier estimate of 1.22 million tonnes.
In its World Horticultural Trade circular, USDA repeated its estimate that Brazil would export 1.16 million tonnes of orange juice in 1997/98.
Most market sources said the Brazilian estimate came as no surprise to the industry.
"We all know its going to be a big crop," said one trader. "It is already in the market and reinforces what we already know."
However, some traders said that while the USDA's forecast was largely priced into the market, the increase could still weigh on prices.
"The market's been down in anticipation of big crops," said another trader, "but I think it will have a psychological effect and could take the market even lower."
Technically, September support was pegged at 73.00 cents and Novemember support was seen at 76.00 cents.
Traders continue to await a private estimate of the 1997/98 Florida crop by Citrus Consulting International, on August 14.
The USDA will issue its Florida crop estimate in October.
